name: m3_consistency_bugfix
stressor: multi-file behavior bug: one invariant (which status codes are RATE_LIMITED and how each layer treats them) is split across 4 modules; a partial fix still fails
source_note: Grounded in urllib3's real retry design, where the set of retryable status codes is split between Retry.status_forcelist and the constant RETRY_AFTER_STATUS_CODES = frozenset([413, 429, 503]), and Retry.is_retry()/get_retry_after() must agree on them (https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/main/src/urllib3/util/retry.py). This is the classic SWE-bench multi-file bug class: a status/retry convention duplicated across modules drifts when one site is updated but not the others (SWE-bench ground-truth patches average ~1.7 files / 3 functions; the hard tail touches 3+ interdependent files -- https://huggingface.co/datasets/princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified). Ported semantics: a 'httpretry' package classifies 429/413 as RATE_LIMITED, but only RetryClass gained the member -- status.classify, policy.is_retryable, backoff._BASE_DELAY and retryafter.honors_retry_after were never wired for it, so a 429 is treated as permanent, KeyErrors in backoff, and ignores Retry-After.
discriminator: The SAME RATE_LIMITED invariant must be threaded into FOUR interdependent files consistently (status.classify maps the codes; policy treats the class as retryable; backoff gives the class a base delay that is strictly larger than TRANSIENT; retryafter honors the class's Retry-After) -- and client.py (untouched) only works when all four agree. A bounded-slice agent holds all four collaborators in its working set and keeps the class wiring identical; a growing-transcript agent tends to fix the symptom it first reproduced (e.g. policy) and leave backoff KeyErroring or retryafter ignoring the header, or it folds 429 into the TRANSIENT code set (a one-file shortcut) which the verifier rejects because RATE_LIMITED must back off more than TRANSIENT. A blanket find-replace of 429/413 also corrupts the statuscodes.py distractor.
